channel.description: This is a randomly ordered feed of the most recent entries from summarizedStoriesMainNLscienceAndDiscovery, skipping any feeds with errors.

item.title: 66-million-year-old feather in dinosaur dung may explain bird survival
item.description: A feather found in 66-million-year-old fossilized dinosaur dung may help explain why modern birds survived the asteroid extinction.

item.title: Bat DNA may hold clues to longer life
item.description: Long-lived bats appear to combine strong immune defenses with unusual ways of clearing damaged cells, possibly helping them avoid cancer.

item.title: Human heart can regrow muscle after heart attack, study finds
item.description: Researchers have demonstrated for the first time that human heart muscle cells can regenerate after a heart attack, challenging the belief that such damage is permanent.

item.title: Wasps vanish this summer, alarming scientists
item.description: Britain's wasps have become mysteriously scarce this summer, with scientists suspecting an unusual mix of temperature swings, heatwaves, and food shortages.
